هِرْبِذَى A proud and self-conceited manner of walking, or going: (L, K;) which a (L.) a manner of waking or going like that of the هَرَابِذَة [pl. of هِرْبِذٌ] (A'Obeyd, 1: A'Obeyd mentions it in speaking of the paces of camels. and says that it is without a parallel in form. (L.) ―
-b2- عَدَا الجَمَلُ الهِرْبِذَى The camel ran in clining towards one side. (S, L, K.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
